rv.q: The Arsonists not only welcomes an award-winning New York director to the City of Angels, it sets the L.A. theater scene on fire like nobody’s business.
Nobody in this play, onstage or off, is equipped to refuse a well-mannered guest.

I admired this production, despite parts of the play annoying me, because its presentation is so artfully conceived; watching skillful actors is never a waste of time; the production design is of a piece; and the event had me brooding and mulling it over long after the lights went down.
It becomes frustrating and tedious, even in a play of only 90 minutes.

cn.t: Max Frisch's absurdist classic receives a strikingly staged, well-performed update that earns mostly positive reviews, though some critics find it sparks more debate about avant-garde theater than the societal issues it addresses.
